profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, which added facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites, not Virginia.

This building, VA-6, at 11891 Sudley Manor Drive, Manassas, Virginia, is part of Iron Mountain's 142-acre Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County, addressed via a different street frontage than VA-1 through VA-5's Hayden Road entrance on the same parcel, per aggregator Baxtel, which independently confirms this address while describing the campus as "one of nine planned data centers" on that 142-acre site, consistent with the operator's own campus-wide buildout figures. Per the operator's own site, the full campus currently comprises seven operational data centers, with a planned buildout of nine to ten buildings totaling more than 2,000,000 square feet and 400-plus MW of capacity, and Iron Mountain has separately acquired an adjacent 40-acre parcel for two further buildings totaling roughly 150 additional MW.

Iron Mountain's own VA-6 location page reuses the same 11680 Hayden Road Google Maps link seen on its VA-2 page, an apparent site-wide template bug also seen elsewhere on the operator's site; this registry relies on Baxtel's distinct, campus-consistent Sudley Manor Drive address instead. Per the operator, VA-6 carries 32 MW of IT capacity across roughly 230,000 gross square feet, in four data halls each over 23,000 square feet, under a "Block N+1" configuration, with referenced certifications including NIST 800-53, FISMA HIGH, FedRAMP, SOC 2 Type II, and multiple ISO standards. The operator states an expected Q3 2025 opening; Baxtel separately confirms a 2025 opening year, "fully operational" status, and NOVEC as the utility provider. No independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate was located for this building.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-6 is a 32 MW data center on the Manassas campus in Prince William County, Virginia, opened in 2025. The 230,000 gross square feet across four halls, stated as "Block N+1" configuration, represents roughly 800 racks at an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common baseline for colocation; higher-density AI training configurations would yield substantially fewer. The facility carries federal compliance certifications including FISMA HIGH and FedRAMP, qualifying it for United States government workloads. No independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate is published for this building.

Virginia publishes capacity figures for 23 data centers totaling 1,375 MW across 326 mapped facilities statewide. VA-6 ranks 24th by published capacity, placing it outside the top tier of published Virginia assets by stated IT load. The Manassas campus itself is planned for nine to ten buildings and over 400 MW total, with an adjacent 40-acre parcel holding two more buildings at roughly 150 additional MW, indicating a multi-year buildout whose final scale remains unfinished.

The utility provider is NOVEC, and the operator states 100% matched renewable power. Published grid constraint data for NOVEC's service territory and the campus's actual renewable sourcing and firm power arrangements are not published. The campus location in Prince William County places it within the broader Northern Virginia data center cluster but distinct from the larger assets in Northern Virginia's primary corridors.
